questions.q: Compared with adult bone, paediatric bone has:
questions.exp: Characteristics of paediatric bones: more water content, thicker periosteum, and potential to remodel and correct deformities and fractures (especially metaphysis). (Book p154)

questions.q: The more water content of paediatric bone makes it:
opts: Flexible and resilient to stress - bends > breaks
questions.exp: More water content: flexible and resilient to stress; bends > breaks. (Book p154)

questions.q: The second characteristic of paediatric bone is:
questions.exp: Characteristic 2: thicker periosteum. (Book p154)

questions.q: The third characteristic of paediatric bone is the potential to:
opts: Remodel and correct deformities and fractures, especially in the metaphysis
questions.exp: Characteristic 3: potential to remodel and correct deformities and fractures (especially metaphysis). (Book p154)

questions.q: When force is applied to the bone within physiological limits:
questions.exp: Force within physiological limits: bone bends. (Book p154)

questions.q: When the bone bends, the outer (convex) surface takes the:
questions.exp: Outer surface: convex -> distractive / tension force; inner surface: concave -> compression force. (Book p154)

questions.q: When force goes beyond physiological limits, breaking of the outer cortex produces a:
questions.exp: Force beyond physiological limits: outer cortex breaks -> greenstick / unicortical fracture. (Book p154)

questions.q: When force goes beyond physiological limits, bulging of the inner surface produces a:
questions.exp: Force beyond physiological limits: inner surface bulges -> torus fracture. (Book p154)

questions.q: As per the notes, the m/c fracture occurring in children is the:
questions.exp: Greenstick fracture: m/c fracture occurring in children. (Book p154)

questions.q: A greenstick fracture is said to mimic:
opts: The stem of a growing tree
A tubular cylinder at the base of a pillar
questions.exp: Greenstick fracture mimics the stem of a growing tree. (Book p154)

questions.q: The common location of the greenstick fracture is the:
questions.exp: Location: radius > ulna. (Book p154)

questions.q: Treatment of the greenstick fracture is:
opts: Break the other intact cortex (osteoclasis) -> realign the bone
questions.exp: Treatment: break the other intact cortex (osteoclasis) -> realign the bone. (Book p154)

questions.q: A torus fracture occurs d/t:
questions.exp: Torus fracture: occurs d/t buckling of bone. (Book p154)

questions.q: A torus fracture resembles:
opts: The stem of a growing tree
A tubular cylinder at the base of a pillar
questions.exp: Torus fracture resembles a tubular cylinder at the base of a pillar. (Book p154)

questions.q: Treatment of the torus fracture is:
questions.exp: Treatment: POP application. (Book p154)

questions.q: The m/c fracture at birth is the fracture of the:
questions.exp: M/c fracture at birth: clavicle. (Book p154)

questions.q: The m/c fracture in a child after a fall on an outstretched hand is the:
questions.exp: M/c fracture in a child after fall on outstretched hand: supracondylar fracture. (Book p154)

questions.q: The m/c fracture overall in children is the fracture of the:
questions.exp: M/c fracture overall: clavicle. (Book p154)

questions.q: Toddler's fracture is a:
questions.exp: Toddler's fracture: spiral fracture of tibia. (Book p155)

questions.q: The etiology of toddler's fracture is:
questions.exp: Etiology: trivial accidents. (Book p155)

questions.q: The fracture pattern in toddler's fracture is typically:
questions.exp: Feature: intact fracture pattern (undisplaced). (Book p155)

questions.q: Toddler's fracture is a well supported fracture d/t the:
questions.exp: Well supported fracture d/t thick periosteum. (Book p155)

questions.q: In toddler's fracture the fibula is intact, so the child:
opts: Presents walking - can bear weight on the fractured bone, with limp d/t pain
Presents with a grossly deformed limb
questions.exp: Fibula is intact so the child can present walking; can bear weight on fractured bone; limp d/t pain. (Book p155)

questions.q: Treatment of toddler's fracture is:
questions.exp: Treatment: POP cast. (Book p155)

questions.q: Battered Baby Syndrome is characterized by all of the following EXCEPT:
opts: Multiple fractures (usually metaphyseal) or bruises in different stages of healing
Long bone fractures in non-ambulatory children
questions.exp: Features: multiple fractures (usually metaphyseal) or bruises in different stages of healing; inconsistent history, signs of neglect; long bone fractures in non-ambulatory children. (Book p155)

questions.q: When Battered Baby Syndrome is suspected, the investigation is:
questions.exp: Suspicion of battered baby syndrome -> X-ray Scanogram. (Book p155)

questions.q: The metaphyseal bucket handle fracture is d/t:
opts: Violent to and fro shaking of children <2 yrs age
questions.exp: Metaphyseal bucket handle fracture: d/t violent to and fro shaking of children <2 yrs age. (Book p155)

questions.q: In the metaphyseal bucket handle fracture, the mechanism results in:
opts: Avulsion of the capsule from the bone
questions.exp: Violent shaking -> avulsion of the capsule from the bone. (Book p155)

questions.q: The typical age group for the metaphyseal bucket handle fracture of shaking is:
questions.exp: Violent to and fro shaking of children <2 yrs age. (Book p155)

questions.q: The direction of growth through the physis is:
questions.exp: Direction of growth: epiphysis to metaphysis. (Book p155)

questions.q: The most important layer of the growth plate is the:
questions.exp: Layers of growth plate: 1. germinal: most important, 2. proliferative, 3. hypertrophic: weakest, 4. calcification, 5. ossification. (Book p155)

questions.q: The weakest layer of the growth plate is the:
questions.exp: Hypertrophic layer: weakest. (Book p155)

questions.q: The correct order of the layers of the growth plate is:
questions.exp: Layers: 1. germinal, 2. proliferative, 3. hypertrophic, 4. calcification, 5. ossification. (Book p155)

questions.q: The germinal zone of the growth plate contains:
questions.exp: Germinal zone: chondrocyte stem cells. (Book p155)

questions.q: Injury affecting the germinal layer impairs growth, leading to:
questions.exp: Injuries affecting germinal layer -> impairs growth -> limb length discrepancy, deformity. (Book p156)

questions.q: In the knee example of partial growth plate damage (restricted growth of the medial condyle), the resulting deformity is:
questions.exp: Example at the knee: damage to only part of the growth plate -> restricted growth of medial condyle, increased growth of lateral condyle -> genu varus deformity. (Book p156)

questions.q: In Salter-Harris Type I (Split fracture):
opts: The fracture splits the growth plate without injuring the germinal layer, with normal growth on reducing the fracture
The fracture line goes towards the metaphysis
The fracture line goes towards the epiphysis
questions.exp: Type I: fracture splits the growth plate without injuring germinal layer; normal growth on reducing the fracture. (Book p156)

questions.q: The m/c type in the Salter-Harris classification is Type:
questions.exp: Type II is the m/c. (Book p156)

questions.q: In Salter-Harris Type II, the fracture line:
opts: Goes only through the germinal layer
Splits the growth plate and goes towards the metaphysis, with no injury to the germinal layer
questions.exp: Type II: fracture splits the growth plate; fracture line goes towards the metaphysis; no injury to the germinal layer; normal growth on reducing the fracture. (Book p156)

questions.q: The metaphyseal fragment seen in Salter-Harris Type II is called:
questions.exp: Type II: metaphyseal fragment: Thurston Holland. (Book p156)

questions.q: The prognosis of Salter-Harris Type I and Type II is:
questions.exp: Type I and II: prognosis good (normal growth on reducing the fracture). (Book p156)

questions.q: Slipped capital femoral epiphysis (SCFE) is an example of Salter-Harris Type:
questions.exp: Type I example: slipped capital femoral epiphysis (SCFE). (Book p156)

questions.q: Supracondylar humerus fracture is an example of Salter-Harris Type:
questions.exp: Type II example: supracondylar humerus fracture. (Book p156)

questions.q: In Salter-Harris Type III, the fracture line:
opts: Splits the growth plate and goes towards the epiphysis; the germinal layer will be injured
questions.exp: Type III: fracture line splits the growth plate and goes towards the epiphysis; germinal layer will be injured; no growth on reducing the fracture. (Book p156)
